scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which falls outside the standard 30-day refund window policy.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Tyrone Jackson and I'm 42. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Tyrone, thank you for reaching out. I understand you've been away and are concerned about this charge. I'd be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide the email address associated with your account and the last four digits of the payment method used?
Sure, the email is t.jackson@email.com and the card ends in 4492.

Thank you, Tyrone. I have successfully verified your account. I can see the subscription cancellation was processed on the 34th day prior to today, which falls just outside our standard '30-Day Satisfaction Guarantee' policy. However, given your account history and the circumstances, I would like to see how I can assist.
I appreciate that. It was a busy trip and I completely missed the notification email until I got home yesterday.

I completely understand. While our policy strictly limits automated refunds to 30 days, I am authorized to issue a one-time courtesy refund for accounts in good standing when a request is made within 45 days of the charge. I am processing that for you now.
That would be fantastic, thank you so much for your help.

You are very welcome, Tyrone. I have successfully issued the refund of $49.99 to your card ending in 4492. You should see the credit reflect in your bank statement within 3-5 business days depending on your financial institution. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the account, acknowledged the policy violation, and utilized an authorized one-time courtesy exception to process the refund for the customer.
